journeyMining.title: Journey Audit
journeyMining.body: Auditing the storefront journey a brand already runs — every public touchpoint captured as customers see it, scored on five dimensions and mapped stage by stage with the handoffs between them. Findings marked OBSERVED come from live pages; traffic and revenue figures stay labelled as estimates until an analytics source replaces them with measured data.
journeyMining.example: “Journey · 14 touchpoints audited · Grade C · 3 broken handoffs”

revenueAtRisk.title: Revenue at risk (mined)
revenueAtRisk.body: What a journey leak costs per month if left alone: affected sessions × the stage’s conversion shortfall × AOV. A mined estimate from connected-source data — labelled as such, and separate from Pulse’s measured numbers, which only ever come from experiences ReXeR actually ran.

journeyCoverage.title: Journey coverage (sources)
journeyCoverage.body: Which funnel stages the connected, healthy sources can actually see. A stage no source illuminates is dark — the miner will not guess at it, and opportunities lose confidence when a source backing their evidence goes down. Coverage ties Sources to Audit quality.
journeyCoverage.example: “5 of 5 stages covered · Klaviyo down → confidence −8”

evidenceSeededDraft.title: Evidence-seeded draft
evidenceSeededDraft.body: A draft built from the mined evidence, not from a blank prompt: every block cites what it leans on, only substantiated claims travel (the unproven one ships as an empty slot with the reason), and the draft is born untracked — below the ship floor — so Ready is still earned, not clicked.
evidenceSeededDraft.example: “Drafted by RxR Agent from ‘TikTok landing mismatch’”

settings.title: Settings
settings.descGeneral: The workspace identity — the organization's name flows into every derived surface that names it.
settings.descMeasurement: The governance layer. These dials are the Measurement Bible's constants: every verdict on every screen derives through them, so a change here reconfigures the platform, live.
settings.descPrivacy: The contract's guardrails. The ceiling bars deeper tiers in every editor's Signal panel; the default follows the ceiling down automatically.
settings.descTeam: Who may turn which dial. Roles are governance, not decoration — an editor builds, a manager ships, an owner rewrites the constants.
settings.descData: The ground truth is yours. Every number on every screen derives from the fact table, and the fact table exports flattened.
settings.toastSaved: Governance saved — every derived verdict follows these values.
settings.toastRestored: Governance dials reset to the Bible's defaults — save to apply.
settings.errOrgName: The organization needs a name — every derived surface names it.
settings.errHighFloor: The High floor must sit above the Directional floor ({floor}).
settings.errDirFloor: The Directional floor must sit between {min} and the High floor ({floor}).
settings.errBlkGap: The swap gap governs a recommendation — keep it between {min} and {max} points.
settings.errWeights: Weights are shares of one verdict — these sum to {sum}, not 100.
settings.errDefPrivacy: The default cannot exceed the workspace ceiling ({tier}).
settings.errOwner: A workspace needs at least one active owner.
settings.hintOrgName: The organization's name flows into every derived surface that names it — the brand space, the shopper preview, the profile.
settings.hintEmailLocked: The sign-in address is changed from your profile, not here.
settings.hintSpaces: The account type is the key into the capability table — change it and the spaces, the seats, and the Exchange gate all follow.
settings.hintProductStatus: A draft is visible to the team only; an active product may be attached to an experience and served.
settings.noteTiers: the floors every chip is judged by
settings.hintHighFloor: Must sit above the Directional floor.
settings.proofLine: The proof, live: "{name}" carries {sessions} sessions and currently wears
settings.hintTiers: Move a floor and every confidence chip on every screen moves with it — the chips and the dials can never disagree.
settings.noteBench: when the engine may recommend a swap
settings.hintBench: Below this bar the swap still exists — it is simply labelled "the graph does not recommend it".
settings.noteWeights: shares of one verdict — must sum to 100
settings.eyebrowScoreWeights: How a page review is composed
settings.eyebrowFitWeights: How a journey stage shops for an experience
settings.hintNotGoverned: Not governed here, on purpose: the block-grain tier ceiling (Directional — no control exists at that grain) and the stale threshold (deployment health is seeded, not date-computed; a dial on it would lie).
settings.fieldDefPrivacy: Default tier for new tracking points
settings.fieldMaxPrivacy: Workspace ceiling — the deepest tier permitted
settings.hintCeiling: Deeper tiers are barred everywhere once the ceiling is set.
settings.hintPrivacy: The ceiling bars deeper tiers in every editor's Signal panel; the default follows the ceiling down automatically. "Meaning before mechanics" is a law, not a setting — there is no dial to turn it off.
settings.privacyFollowed: The default tier followed the ceiling down to {tier}.
settings.hintLaw: A barred tier cannot be selected anywhere in the workspace — not in an editor, not by an import, not by an API key.
settings.toastInviteSoon: Invitations ship with the identity service.
settings.hintPeople: Only an owner may turn the governance dials. Everyone else reads them, so nobody argues with a number they cannot see.

settings.noteFacts: sample data, not your real measurements yet
